facts.text: A Proximity Detection System (PDS) senses when a person or machine comes within a set distance of a machine and warns or stops the machine; the term is used mainly in US underground coal mining and in South Africa.
facts.quote: A Proximity Detection System (PDS) senses when a person or machine comes within a set distance of a machine and warns or stops it; the term is used mainly in US underground coal mining and in South Africa.

facts.text: Many Proximity Detection System (PDS) designs are tag-based: workers wear a small transmitter, and the machine measures how close each tag is.
facts.quote: Many PDS designs are tag-based: workers wear a small transmitter and the machine measures how close each tag is.

facts.text: A 2015 US rule requires proximity detection on continuous mining machines to stop the machine before the machine contacts a miner.
facts.quote: A 2015 US rule requires proximity detection on continuous mining machines to stop the machine before it contacts a miner [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The underground Proximity Detection System (PDS) record is the richest field evidence of what happens when a system can stop a machine.
facts.quote: The underground PDS record is the richest field evidence of what happens when a system can stop a machine.

facts.text: Workers at seven coal mines reported that mobile Proximity Detection Systems (PDS) unnecessarily shut down vehicles from once a day to 15 times during a single cut of coal.
facts.quote: Workers at seven coal mines said mobile PDS "unnecessarily shut down vehicles anywhere from once a day up to 15 times during a single cut of coal,"

facts.text: Nearly 70% of workers surveyed at seven coal mines worried about how and when mobile Proximity Detection Systems (PDS) take control.
facts.quote: Workers at seven coal mines said mobile PDS "unnecessarily shut down vehicles anywhere from once a day up to 15 times during a single cut of coal," and nearly 70% worried about "how and when the mobile PDS takes control" [Chapter 4].

facts.text: At one mine, the Proximity Detection System emergency-stop override had become routine; a worker had used the override 87 times before his fatal accident in 2017.
facts.quote: At one mine the emergency-stop override had become routine and had been used 87 times by a worker before his fatal accident in 2017 [Chapter 4].

facts.text: NIOSH judged that proximity systems might have prevented 82% of 39 continuous-miner deaths.
facts.quote: NIOSH judged that 82% of 39 continuous-miner deaths might have been prevented by proximity systems [Chapter 4]

facts.text: NIOSH developed an intelligent Proximity Detection System (PDS) that blocks only the machine motions that could pin a worker.
facts.quote: developed "intelligent" PDS that blocks only the motions that could pin a worker [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The Proximity Detection System (PDS) industry's experience with nuisance stops, overrides and bypasses is the booklet's main warning about what an automatic brake must avoid.
facts.quote: PDS is where the industry has already lived through nuisance stops, overrides and bypasses, so its record is the booklet's main warning about what an automatic brake must avoid [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Tag-dependent Proximity Detection Systems (PDS) cannot detect an untagged person, illustrating the limit of cooperative systems.
facts.quote: Its tag dependence also shows the limit of cooperative systems: an untagged person is invisible.
